### 2026-09-25 — Admin "Renew now": force a specific customer's renewal immediately, wallet then saved card

**The gap.** `/admin/servers/[id]` had no way to trigger a renewal at all. The only two renewal paths
were `renewNow` (`lib/actions.ts`) — customer-facing, wallet-only, no card fallback — and
`renewDueServer` (`worker/billing.ts`) — the unattended 10-minute sweep, wallet-then-card, but
module-private, gated on `server.autoRenew`, only ever runs on already-expired servers, and returns
nothing a UI could show. Business driver: as of this audit exactly ONE renewal in production history
had ever completed via the card leg (a $2.99 hosting-addon on an internal test account) — zero real
VPS/game-server plan renewals had ever been proven to go through the wallet→card fallback. The owner
wanted a real, repeatable way to trigger and verify it for a specific customer, and to be able to
settle a renewal a little early when operationally sensible.

**Built on `feat/admin-renew-now`, in an isolated worktree (`/root/nxeon-worktrees/admin-renew-now`
— never built against the live `/opt/nxeon` tree). Not pushed or deployed; committed to the branch only.**

**`renewServerImmediately` (worker/billing.ts, new, exported)** — the money mechanics, reusing the
real primitives `renewDueServer` already uses (`walletSplit`, `hasChargeableCard`,
`attemptCardRenewal`, `commitRenewal`, all unmodified in their own logic) rather than a third copy of
the split-then-fallback arithmetic. Deliberately NOT a call into `renewDueServer` itself — two real
differences justified a separate function: (1) `renewDueServer` only attempts a charge when
`server.autoRenew` is true, which would silently no-op an admin's explicit trigger for any customer
who has turned auto-renew off; (2) it returns `void`, useless for a UI that has to say which rail
paid what. `attemptCardRenewal`'s return type was broadened from a bare `boolean` to a new exported
`CardRenewalOutcome` (declined reason/message/code, or the captured amount) so the admin path can
surface a real Stripe decline instead of a generic failure — `renewDueServer`'s own one call site was
updated to read `.renewed` and its behavior is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged (verified: the same
1499 pre-existing tests, same 37 pre-existing unrelated failures, before and after). Also
deliberately unchanged from the sweep: the dunning-retry schedule gate is skipped (an admin click IS
the attempt), and — unlike `dueServers()` — there is no `expiresAt`-has-passed filter, so an early
renewal is a supported, deliberate case, exactly as safe as a late one via the same CAS-on-`expiresAt`
already inside `commitRenewal`.

**`adminRenewServerNow` (lib/actions.ts, new)** — `requireAdmin()`-gated, fetches the server fresh
with the SAME `include` shape `dueServers()` uses (`plan`, `user`, `gamePlan`, `dedicatedIp`) and
hands that RAW row straight to `renewServerImmediately`, deliberately avoiding `renewNow`'s other
pattern (a fresh literal `PricedServer` object) — that pattern is exactly how `annualDiscountPct` /
`grandfatheredRenewalCents` were silently dropped once, per `renewNow`'s own doc comment; passing the
raw row through carries every column, including those two, automatically. Guards: the same
one-in-flight-job check `serverAction` uses (refuses alongside a DELETE/MIGRATE job), free/no-expiry
short-circuit. Deliberately does NOT enforce the owner's spend cap the way the customer's own
`renewNow` does — this action stands in for the automatic sweep, which has never checked it either.
On success: audit-logs `admin.renew_now` with the rail/amounts, runs the same post-charge bookkeeping
`renewNow` runs (partner commission accrual, budget alert), and auto-restores an UNPAID-suspended
server exactly like a customer's own payment would. On failure: audit-logs the attempt too, and
returns the real Stripe decline message/code rather than a generic error.

**UI.** `AdminRenewNowButton` (`components/SubscriptionControls.tsx`) in the "Admin actions" panel of
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, next to `SuspendServerButton`/`ExtendForm`. Before charging, a
`window.confirm` shows the real total and the real wallet/card split — computed server-side in the
page via the SAME `renewalQuote`/`walletSplit` calls the action itself charges through, never a
second estimate (the page's `user` select was extended with balance/card display columns for this).
Disabled when the split would leave a shortfall with no chargeable card, so the confirm dialog is
never reached for a charge already known to fail.

**Real, not just reasoned-about, verification.** Typecheck clean; `npm run build` clean (isolated
worktree, its own throwaway Postgres database `nxeon_verify` and `.env` — never staging, never
production); full suite 1522/1522 collected, 1485 passing, the identical 37 pre-existing unrelated
failures confirmed by diffing the failing-test-name list against a fresh run of unmodified `main` in
the same worktree (`git stash` / run / `git stash pop`), byte-for-byte identical. 23 new tests in
`test/admin-renew-now.test.ts`, following this repo's established split for a "use server"/worker
module that imports `./db` (`test/money-core-guards.test.ts`, `test/retention-offer.test.ts`): real,
executed arithmetic tests composing the actual `renewalCharge` + `walletSplit` functions against
admin-relevant fixtures (grandfathered price, retention discount, annual discount, game plan), plus
source-text tripwires (comments stripped) asserting the two new functions call the primitives, guards
and audit log they claim to, and do not reintroduce the field-dropping bug.

Beyond unit tests: `scripts/verify-admin-renew-now.ts` (new, real, kept in the repo — not part of
`npm test`, same reason the standard suite avoids importing `./db`) stood up the throwaway
`nxeon_verify` Postgres database and called `renewServerImmediately` directly against real rows, with
Stripe's real TEST-mode API (`sk_test_…`, the same key staging uses) — genuinely executed, not
mocked, 9/9 scenarios passing: wallet-only; **wallet+card split producing a real captured Stripe
PaymentIntent** (`pi_3UJZeGHxcLe3GonT02rNkova`, `WalletTransaction.stripePaymentIntentId` populated —
the first VPS/game-server-shaped proof this path works at all); insufficient balance with no card;
a REAL Stripe decline (`"Your card was declined." / code "generic_decline"`, dunning stage advanced,
customer notification queued); two concurrent calls against the same server racing the CAS on
`expiresAt` — exactly one winner, one `alreadyRenewed` loser, exactly one `WalletTransaction` row (no
double charge); grandfathered price honored over the live catalog price; retention discount honored
and cleared after use; game-plan flat price honored over the base VPS plan; and an early renewal (6
hours before expiry) succeeding. The script refuses to run unless `DATABASE_URL` resolves to
`nxeon_verify` by name and `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` starts with `sk_test_`, on purpose — while wiring up
this verification the exact hazard `scripts/db-target-guard.ts` documents recurred live (Prisma's
generated client resolved `/opt/nxeon/.env`'s real Stripe key through the worktree's symlinked
`node_modules`, despite an explicitly-set, correct `DATABASE_URL`), and this refusal caught it before
any Stripe call happened; every run after that passed every secret as an explicit environment
variable rather than trusting ambient `.env` resolution at all.

**Files touched:** `worker/billing.ts`, `lib/actions.ts`, `components/SubscriptionControls.tsx`,
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, plus `test/admin-renew-now.test.ts` and
`scripts/verify-admin-renew-now.ts` (new).

---

*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
(server migration).*

and the automatic sweep's module-private renewDueServer (gated on

could show). As of this audit exactly one renewal in production history
had ever completed via the card leg -- the owner wanted a real,
repeatable way to trigger and verify the wallet->card fallback for a
specific customer, and to be able to settle a renewal a little early
when operationally sensible.

worker/billing.ts: new exported renewServerImmediately(server, ctx),

renewDueServer itself: that function no-ops when autoRenew is off and
returns void. attemptCardRenewal's return type was broadened from a
bare boolean to CardRenewalOutcome so a real Stripe decline reason
reaches the caller; its one existing call site was updated to read
.renewed, with byte-for-byte unchanged sweep behavior (verified).

hands the raw row straight to renewServerImmediately -- avoiding
renewNow's other pattern (a fresh literal PricedServer object), which
is exactly how annualDiscountPct/grandfatheredRenewalCents were
silently dropped once per renewNow's own comment. Guards against a
busy in-flight job, audit-logs both outcomes, does not enforce the
customer's spend cap (this stands in for the sweep, which never has).

for the wallet+card split, a real Stripe decline, and concurrent calls
proving exactly one charge lands.

content.text:
Everything checks out. Here's the full summary of what was built and verified.

## What was built

Branch `feat/admin-renew-now` (commit `b07d75d7c7`) on an isolated worktree at `/root/nxeon-worktrees/admin-renew-now`, off `main` at `549e3a5eac`. Not pushed, not deployed — the post-commit hook only re-pushes local `main` (confirmed: `git ls-remote --heads origin feat/admin-renew-now` is empty).

**`worker/billing.ts`** — new exported `renewServerImmediately(server, ctx)`, the money mechanics. It reuses the sweep's real primitives (`walletSplit`, `hasChargeableCard`, `attemptCardRenewal`, `commitRenewal`) rather than a third copy of the split-then-fallback arithmetic. It deliberately does **not** call `renewDueServer` directly — I checked both real reasons the task asked me to think through: `renewDueServer` only attempts a charge when `server.autoRenew` is true (would silently no-op for any customer who turned it off), and it returns `void` (useless for a UI). I broadened `attemptCardRenewal`'s return from a bare `boolean` to a new exported `CardRenewalOutcome` so a real Stripe decline reason reaches the caller — the sweep's one call site was updated to read `.renewed`, and I verified byte-for-byte unchanged sweep behavior.

**`lib/actions.ts`** — new `adminRenewServerNow(serverId)`, `requireAdmin()`-gated, fetches the server with the exact `include` shape `dueServers()` uses and hands the **raw row** straight to `renewServerImmediately` — deliberately avoiding `renewNow`'s other pattern (a hand-built literal object), which is exactly how `annualDiscountPct`/`grandfatheredRenewalCents` were silently dropped once per that function's own comment. Guards against a busy in-flight job, audit-logs both outcomes (`admin.renew_now`), and deliberately does **not** enforce the spend cap (documented reasoning: this stands in for the automatic sweep, which never has).

**UI** — `AdminRenewNowButton` in `components/SubscriptionControls.tsx`, wired into the Admin actions panel of `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, showing a real wallet/card-split preview computed server-side via the same `renewalQuote` the action itself charges through.

## Verification

- Full suite: 1522 tests, 1485 passing, **same 37 pre-existing failures** — confirmed fresh by `git stash`-ing my changes and diffing the failing-test-name list against unmodified `main` in the same worktree (byte-for-byte identical).
- 23 new tests in `test/admin-renew-now.test.ts`, following this repo's established convention for a `"use server"`/worker module that imports `./db`: real executed arithmetic (composing `renewalCharge` + `walletSplit`) plus source-text tripwires.
- **Real end-to-end verification** in `scripts/verify-admin-renew-now.ts` against an isolated throwaway Postgres database (`nxeon_verify`) and Stripe **TEST mode** (`sk_test_...`, the same key staging uses) — 9/9 scenarios genuinely executed: wallet-only, **wallet+card split producing a real captured PaymentIntent** (`pi_3UJZeGHxcLe3GonT02rNkova`, `WalletTransaction.stripePaymentIntentId` populated — the first VPS/game-server-shaped proof this path works), insufficient-balance-no-card, a real Stripe decline, concurrent double-calls (exactly one winner, one charge), grandfathered price, retention discount, game-plan pricing, and an early (pre-expiry) renewal.
- Along the way I hit the exact node_modules-symlink `.env` hazard this repo's own `scripts/db-target-guard.ts` documents — Prisma's client silently resolved `/opt/nxeon/.env`'s real Stripe key despite an explicit `DATABASE_URL`. My safety check caught it before any wrong-target call happened; all subsequent runs passed every secret as an explicit env var. Documented in the commit and in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

The throwaway `nxeon_verify` database is still around (harmless, isolated) — drop it with `sudo -u postgres psql -c "DROP DATABASE nxeon_verify;"` if not needed.

result: Built and committed (not pushed/deployed) admin-only "Renew now" for `/admin/servers/[id]` on branch `feat/admin-renew-now` — wallet-then-card renewal reusing real billing primitives; full suite unchanged (same 37 pre-existing failures) plus 23 new tests; real Stripe test-mode e2e verification (9/9 scenarios, including a genuine captured PaymentIntent and a real decline) against an isolated throwaway database.
